article_content: UK parliamentary health committee chair Sarah Wollaston advocates for annual weight monitoring of primary school students to combat escalating childhood obesity. Current policy mandates measurements only upon school entry (ages 4-5) and exit (age 11), missing critical growth periods. Data shows 22.2% of Reception children were overweight in 2012-13, rising to 33.3% by Year 6. Wollaston cites parental unawareness as a key challenge, referencing studies where most parents misjudge their child’s weight. The National Health Service spends £5 billion annually managing obesity-related conditions, with hospital admissions for such cases surging from 1,117 to over 3,100 in a decade. Critics like Conservative MP Philip Davies argue the proposal constitutes excessive state intervention. While local authorities may implement additional checks, national policy remains unchanged. New nutritional standards require schools to provide daily milk and limit fruit juice consumption to 150ml daily due to dental health risks, alongside expanding physical activity programs funded through £1.2 million initiatives.

article_content: PHNOM PENH, Cambodia (CNN) -- Youk Chhang knows the truth about the Cambodian genocide perhaps better than anyone in the world. As director of the Documentation Center of Cambodia (DC-Cam), he oversees records of nearly 200 prisons and over 20,000 mass graves. At 13, he survived the Khmer Rouge: torn from his family, enslaved, and nearly killed for stealing rice to aid his pregnant sister. His mother lost five relatives to the genocide; 30 years later, she still seeks them. Chhang scavenged to survive, later fleeing to the U.S. after the regime's collapse. 'Food mattered more than God,' he recalls. 'A bowl of rice and rest were my only desires.' Returning to Cambodia, Chhang founded DC-Cam to preserve genocide archives—documents, photos, and testimonies from both victims and perpetrators. He argues the regime tracked deaths as 'progress,' now used as evidence in trials of five surviving leaders. Chhang hopes these trials will aid Cambodia's healing, though divisions linger: some want to forget, others pursue justice. Dedicated to his mother's strength, he believes truth alone can reconcile the nation's past and future.

Jeho matka ztratila pět příbuzných; po 30 letech stále hledá jejich stopy. Chhang přežil tím, že hledal potravu, později uprchl do USA po pádu režimu. 'Jídlo bylo důležitější než Bohu', vzpomíná. 'Chtěl jsem jen mísu rýže a klidný spánek.' Návrat do Kambodže ho vedl k založení DC-Cam, které chrání dokumenty, fotografie a výpovědi obětí i bývalých členů Khmerské rudy. Chhang doufá, že tyto soudy pomohou zemi uzdravit se, ale rozpory trvají: někteří chtějí zapomenout, ostatní vyžadují spravedlnost. article_content: Wicked Campervans' provocative slogans and graphic artwork have sparked widespread condemnation following the company's ironic defense in media interviews. 'Things are much more fun once they've been banned', claimed representatives after Sydney mother Paula Orbea initiated a Change.org petition with over 100,000 supporters. The petition responds to her daughter encountering a vehicle displaying the slogan 'In every princess, there's a little slut who wants to try it just once'. Spokesperson Leanne Webb (formerly Liam) stated during an SBS interview: 'We don't set out to be controversial... we just enjoy creating what we love.' Despite the backlash, the company remains unfazed, asserting the controversy itself serves as effective 'global marketing'. Queensland legislators are now debating potential bans. While some vans feature slogans, others operate without branded messaging. Over 60 Advertising Standards Bureau complaints have been filed against the firm, though many were dismissed. Critics argue the content perpetuates harmful stereotypes.
